mapping.heading: ## On Codex CLI
lines: JBIT was written for Claude Code; this copy is generated for OpenAI Codex CLI. Where the text or the hook's messages use Claude's names, read them this way:

- **Skills.** Invoke a `jbit:<name>` skill by typing `$jbit:<name>` (for example `$jbit:plan`); that is the form Codex recognises. A typed `/jbit:<name>` or `$<name>` isn't an invocation: the model may find the skill from its description, but nothing guarantees it. When a skill says to run another JBIT skill, open that skill's `SKILL.md` and follow it.

- **Agents.** An Agent call is Codex's `spawn_agent`: `task_name` (lowercase letters, digits and underscores) and `message` (the brief) are required. Pass `model` and `reasoning_effort` only as the plan's Models line sets them, and leave out what it doesn't set; the child then inherits the session's. Give a verifier or reviewer `fork_turns: "none"`, so it starts without this session's history and sees only the brief and the code. Wait with `wait_agent`; `send_message`, `followup_task`, `list_agents` and `interrupt_agent` steer it. JBIT's role agents don't ship on Codex: brief a plain `spawn_agent` with the role.

- **No worktree isolation.** `spawn_agent` has no `isolation: "worktree"`. Build leaves one at a time in the main tree, or in parallel only when each builder owns files no other touches; there is no branch to merge back.
- **Questions.** Where a skill says to ask the user (AskUserQuestion on Claude Code), ask in the chat and wait for the reply.

- **Reviews.** `/code-review` and `/security-review` are Claude Code commands. Here, run a fresh `spawn_agent` with `fork_turns: "none"`, briefed with the same lenses (correctness, then security), and triage what it finds.
- **Instructions.** Codex loads `AGENTS.md`, not `CLAUDE.md`. Where a skill reads or writes `CLAUDE.md`, use that file, and read it yourself at the start of a session.

- **Hooks.** JBIT's hooks run only once the user trusts them (at startup or through `/hooks`), and again after every JBIT update. Without trust there is no `## Now` in context, no gates and no carry-on, and nothing says so.

- **Script paths.** `<verify skill folder>` in a skill's command is a placeholder: put in the folder holding the verify skill's `SKILL.md` in the installed JBIT plugin, never a path inside the project (a project's own `scripts/capture.mjs` isn't JBIT's). Run the script by that full path from the project, so its other paths (`--out docs/evidence/…`) stay relative to the project.
- **Tools.** {tools}. Edits go through `apply_patch`; the guard covers it and the shell alike.

gaps.what: Hooks need trusting after every install and update
gaps.why: Codex runs a plugin's hooks only once the user trusts them, at startup ("Hooks need review", then "Trust all") or through `/hooks`, and every JBIT update voids that trust silently. Until they're trusted again, JBIT has no `## Now` in context, no gates and no carry-on, and nothing says so; `codex exec` skips untrusted hooks without a warning. Trusted hooks run outside the sandbox.

A PreToolUse hook that Codex kills on its 30-second timeout lets the call run. The shipped hook refuses by its own 25-second watchdog first, and refuses when its own modules fail to load, so this bites only if the hook's event loop blocks.

gaps.what: Stall detection and other in-memory state
gaps.why: Each hook event is a fresh process, as on Copilot, so nothing counts repeated turn ends; the hook's own cap of 8 Stop blocks per prompt bounds the loop instead, and an unattended `codex exec` run stops quietly when it's reached. Prompt again to carry on.

gaps.what: Lean's count of agents already running
gaps.why: The Claude hook keeps it in memory across events; a command hook has no running process to keep it in.
Same reason: no in-memory agent list between events.

gaps.what: The reopen check after a commit
gaps.why: It runs before the commit lands, since there's no in-memory state carried to the next event.
JBIT passes at most 40 lines of `## Now` into context, as on Claude Code: a longer one reaches the model cut at its 40th line. Keep `## Now` short.
Codex hands the hook the brief (`message`) encrypted, so no check can read it. The stage hold and the Models line still apply to the call; nothing that needs the brief's words does.
The hooks fire for `Bash` and `apply_patch` calls a subagent makes, but whether they fire for its `write_stdin` and MCP tool calls is unproven.

gaps.what: Writes through the shell in a held stage
gaps.why: The hold refuses `apply_patch` and builder agents, but a file written by a shell command (`echo > file`, `sed -i`) isn't held, on any host: the hook can't tell a build step from a read in a shell line.

Writes under `$CODEX_HOME` or a `.codex` folder are refused through `apply_patch` and through shell commands that name the folder, but the shell check is best-effort: a command that reaches the folder without naming it isn't caught.
The guard compares paths case-sensitively, so on a case-insensitive file system (macOS, Windows) a write to `.Codex/` or to `$CODEX_HOME` spelled in another case can slip past it.
A Codex plugin can't register agents, so the package ships none; builders, verifiers and reviewers are plain `spawn_agent` calls briefed with the role.
Codex loads `AGENTS.md`, not `CLAUDE.md`; the skills tell the model to read `CLAUDE.md` itself.

Codex recognises a skill only as `$jbit:<name>` (for example `$jbit:autopilot`). A typed `/jbit:plan` or `$plan` reaches the model as plain text, which may still find the skill from its description, with no guarantee. The hook reads a leading `$jbit:autopilot` or `$jbit:approve` as the typed command.
The hook runs the Claude hook's TypeScript through Node's type stripping; an older Node can't load it, so guarded tool calls are refused.
They are Claude Code built-ins; on Codex the review runs as a fresh `spawn_agent` briefed with the same lenses.
Codex's `spawn_agent` has none, so parallel builders must own separate files or run one at a time.

gaps.what: Compacting the context before autopilot carries on
gaps.why: Codex gives a command hook no context gauge and no compact call; Codex manages its own context.
They are the Claude hook's words and name Claude tools (Agent, Edit, Write); each skill's mapping section translates them.

In a `codex exec` run under `--sandbox workspace-write`, Chromium could not start (it aborted at launch with `shutdown: Operation not permitted`), so `capture.mjs` stopped with "The browser would not launch"; with the sandbox off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`) the same script took the screenshot. So run it outside the workspace-write sandbox (with Codex's approval, or a full-access sandbox such as `--sandbox danger-full-access`). Finding the script works: the model fills `<verify skill folder>/scripts/capture.mjs` from the `SKILL.md` path Codex lists for the skill.
